name: Nutlope/hallmark
description: Anti-AI-slop design skill for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.
readmeExcerpt: Hallmark **A design skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode that refuses to look AI-generated.** usehallmark.com  ·  fifty themes  ·  custom on request  ·  redesign and audit by name Made by Together AI. Hallmark holds a hard floor and then gets out of the way. It deals three themes from a catalog of fifty materials, builds the page around what the visitor came to do, and lints the result in a real browser against the tells that read as machine-made: the eyebrow above every heading, tracked-capital labels, one coloured word in a headline, a page of empty frames or nothing but photographs, a hero that misses its screen, an email sign-up at the end of every page, a form that says thanks without sending anything. A fresh-context reviewer gets the last word. The gates come in tiers. The **Floor** never ships (contrast, focus, reduced motion, invented facts, a broken phone layout). **Reflex** gates are the defaults a model falls into; a build with a reason may overrule one on the record. **Finish** checks are craft detail that never blocks a ship. description: A local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates. Run Codex, Claude, and Grok with dedicated workspaces, task queues, file sharing, browser control, and agent-to-agent collaboration.
readmeExcerpt: OpenBot OpenBot is a local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates. It supports the local Codex App Server and Claude Code, plus Grok CLI, OpenCode, Gemini, Cursor CLI, and Cline CLI through ACP. It gives every agent its own workspace and conversation, and provides local queues, file transfers, an embedded browser, and agent-to-agent messaging in one desktop app. > [!WARNING] > OpenBot is a development preview. Agents currently run with `danger-full-access` and > `approvalPolicy: never`. They can read and modify files, run commands, use the network, and control > the embedded browser without per-action confirmations after the explicit first-launch consent. > Run only agents and tasks you trust, keep backups, and review Security before use. name: obra/superpowers
description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.
readmeExcerpt: Superpowers Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them. Table of Contents - How it works - Commercial Services - Getting Started - Claude Code - Antigravity - Codex App - Codex CLI - Cursor - Devin CLI - Factory Droid - Gemini CLI - GitHub Copilot CLI - Grok Build CLI - Kimi Code - OpenCode - Pi - Qwen Code - Hermes Agent - Muse - The Basic Workflow - When Something Goes Wrong - Community - What's Inside - Philosophy - Contributing - Updating - License - Visual companion telemetry How it works It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it *doesn't* just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do. Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest. name: JetBrains/thinkrail
description: Vibe code with pi in a lightweight, real IDE that customises itself around the way you work — The Vibe You Need
readmeExcerpt: ThinkRail ThinkRail is the agentic IDE that gets better every time you use it — learning your project through living specs today, and building its own capabilities tomorrow. We built a rich interface around the `pi` coding agent, isolated work into separate workspaces, and gave the agent durable project knowledge through living specs and reusable skills. Next, we're adding full extension support, so ThinkRail can create the tools it needs based on how you actually work. **Website:** thinkrail.ai · **Blog:** thinkrail.ai/blog · **Discord:** thinkrail.ai/discord ⭐ If you find ThinkRail useful, give it a star — it helps others discover it. *A `pi` session and the change it made, scoped to an isolated git-worktree workspace.* What you get - **Isolated workspaces.** Open any git repo as a project and cut workspaces from it as `git worktree`s, each with its own branch and working directory. Agents work in parallel without touching your checkout; merge the good branch, delete the rest. You can also attach existing worktrees or explicitly work in the project folder itself.
